E01.input_contract: Preserve record/source locator, study, design, observation ID, experimental-unit ID (nullable), specimen/pool ID, technical-repeat ID, regimen and dose occasion, route/formulation, analyte, matrix, free/total basis, time value/unit/origin, measured value/unit and quantification status. Map only available applicable fields; never invent missing identities. Preserve nullable serial_observation_subject_id separately from experimental_unit_id, with its source linkage. Numeric measured value is required only for quantified records; censoring/missing statuses may have a null numeric value. Optional summary/error inputs are needed only when that layer is displayed.
E01.plot_type: Individual concentration-time scatter with optional verified serial lines; linear and positive-only log-y companion panels.
E01.axes_and_units: X = actual elapsed time from a documented reference event, in stated units; Y = measured concentration on its stated analyte/matrix/free-total basis and unit. Time since last dose requires verified dose history and dose occasion; retain global documented time for traceability. Positive-only log-y is optional; measured zero remains on the linear panel.
E01.grouping_and_connections: Separate study, regimen/dose occasion, route/formulation, analyte/matrix/basis and endpoint contexts. Connect only verified serial observations of the same unit in a compatible time reference, ordered by time. Break connections at recorded unresolved missing/censored statuses. No invented scheduled samples or cross-unit lines. Serial-observation subject ID is distinct from experimental-unit ID: a cage/litter may contain several animals. Individual trajectories or paired loops require the same verified serial_observation_subject_id within study and compatible regimen/time/assay context. A shared cage/litter ID alone never authorizes connecting animals. Unknown serial identity blocks individual lines/pairs, not record-level displays; unknown experimental-unit identity blocks independent-unit n/uncertainty, not an otherwise verified observed subject series.
E01.point_and_summary_layers: Preserve observed values as points at their actual record level. Keep raw observations separate from optional source-reported or explicitly defined descriptive summaries. A labelled group-summary guide is not an individual trajectory. Do not reconstruct individuals from a mean and SD.
E01.censoring_and_missingness: Separate quantified, BLQ, confirmed above-range, missing, not sampled and technical-failure states. BLQ is not zero or negative. Confirmed BLQ implies C < LLOQ; confirmed above-range implies C > ULOQ. Default engineering convention: categorical status strip; optional boundary markers require known applicable limits and explicit inequality. No substitution or silent exclusion.
E01.transformations_and_formula: Retain original values, units, formula, input linkage and calculation order. Perform only the explicitly stated descriptive transformation with complete compatible inputs. No model fitting, integration, unsampled-peak interpolation or arbitrary log offsets.
E01.uncertainty_and_n: Label displayed record counts separately from known independent experimental-unit n. Preserve supplied statistic, calculation scale and exact SD, SE or CI meaning, including asymmetric interval endpoints. Technical repeats do not increase biological n. Unknown n or variability stays unknown; no automatic CI or zero-width bar.
E01.interpretation_limits: A semilog visual slope is not a terminal elimination estimate or evidence for a compartment structure. Missingness mechanism is unknown from this plot; visual patterns neither select covariates nor qualify model feasibility.
E01.stop_or_fallback: Block only the operation that needs an unresolved input. Unknown serial-subject IDs block individual connections; unknown experimental-unit IDs block independent-unit summaries. Neither blocks labelled observed record/group displays. Unknown limits block numeric boundary placement, not status display. Unknown time origin permits a source timestamp only if documented; otherwise use a record table. Missing validation documentation means qualification unestablished, not automatically invalid. Serial-observation subject ID is distinct from experimental-unit ID: a cage/litter may contain several animals. Individual trajectories or paired loops require the same verified serial_observation_subject_id within study and compatible regimen/time/assay context. A shared cage/litter ID alone never authorizes connecting animals. Unknown serial identity blocks individual lines/pairs, not record-level displays; unknown experimental-unit identity blocks independent-unit n/uncertainty, not an otherwise verified observed subject series.
E01.implementation_conventions: This recipe is an explicitly reviewed engineering display contract, not a regulator-mandated layout or scientific law. Use readable legends, separate aligned panels and visible status/count annotations. No universal numeric completeness threshold. No change to source data or current project Rules.

E08.input_contract: Choose independent branches, never require both: binding needs concentration with nominal-added versus measured stage, named bound/unbound fraction or percent, species/matrix/assay conditions and sample/run identities. Depletion needs incubation time, measured parent concentration or established remaining fraction, documented reference relation and assay-series/run/replicate identities. Preserve independent experimental-run ID separately from analytical series, specimen/aliquot and technical-repeat IDs. Numeric measured values are required only for quantified records; status-only records can have null numeric value. Optional summaries/errors need their own defined inputs.
E08.plot_type: Separate conditional binding scatter and depletion-time plot; either may be shown independently.
E08.axes_and_units: Binding: X = clearly defined assay concentration and unit, Y = explicitly bound or unbound fraction (0-1) or percent (0-100), without silently rescaling out-of-range observations. Depletion: X = incubation time/unit; Y = measured parent concentration/unit or established percent remaining. Label assay/species/matrix and known conditions.
E08.grouping_and_connections: Separate assay series, experimental run, species/matrix, binding method and reference definitions. Use verified analytical_series_id and specimen/aliquot linkage, not an animal-subject ID by default. A same-series depletion guide may link documented successive observations; destructive aliquots must be labelled as a series/group guide, not a repeated specimen trajectory. Technical repeats are nested and do not create independent experimental runs.
E08.point_and_summary_layers: Preserve observed values as points at their actual record level. Keep raw observations separate from optional source-reported or explicitly defined descriptive summaries. A labelled group-summary guide is not an individual trajectory. Do not reconstruct individuals from a mean and SD.
E08.censoring_and_missingness: Binding: preserve bound versus unbound fraction/percent, the actual concentration-stage definition and assay-specific qualification/status; an out-of-range fraction is flagged, not clipped or relabelled concentration BLQ. Depletion: retain measured parent concentration status and its actual assay limits. A bound on C_t can be converted to a percent bound only with a documented positive compatible C_ref and inequality propagation. Missing reference blocks normalization only; no zero/half-limit substitution or silent deletion. A censored or uncertain reference is not an exact denominator: retain its status/interval and use normalization only with a qualified uncertainty/interval propagation method. Positivity alone does not qualify a reference as exact.
E08.transformations_and_formula: Bound and unbound fractions are distinct assay-defined quantities, not interchangeable labels. Only with established numerator/denominator definitions convert fraction to percent by multiplying by 100. For a documented compatible reference qualified for quantitative normalization, percent remaining = 100*C_t/C_ref. Direct pointwise division requires a qualified positive quantified reference, with no unhandled uncertainty or censoring; an uncertain/censored reference requires a qualified uncertainty/interval propagation method instead of silently treating it as exact. C_ref need not be a newly invented t=0 measurement. Retain reference linkage, assay recovery/mass-balance qualifications and raw values.
E08.uncertainty_and_n: Label displayed record counts separately from known independent experimental-unit n. Preserve supplied statistic, calculation scale and exact SD, SE or CI meaning, including asymmetric interval endpoints. Technical repeats do not increase independent experimental-run or other documented design-unit n; cell-free assays do not require an animal/biological n label. Unknown n or variability stays unknown; no automatic CI or zero-width bar.
E08.interpretation_limits: Plasma/serum binding does not automatically supply incubation binding. The display does not itself fit a depletion slope or estimate CLint; a separate qualified downstream method may do so. No source drug values transfer to the current target.
E08.stop_or_fallback: Unknown or nonpositive C_ref blocks percent normalization only: show qualified raw concentration versus incubation time. Unknown assay validation documentation means qualification unestablished, not automatic plotting prohibition. A separately valid binding branch remains available. Unresolved series/run linkage blocks connections or independent-run summaries only, not labelled observed assay records. If reference uncertainty/censoring has no qualified propagation method, retain raw concentration and reference status, omit the dependent normalized value/bound, and state why.
E08.implementation_conventions: This recipe is an explicitly reviewed engineering display contract, not a regulator-mandated layout or scientific law. Use readable legends, separate aligned panels and visible status/count annotations. No universal numeric completeness threshold. No change to source data or current project Rules.
